subject_name: Aircraft Husbandry, Corrosion Prevention and Surface Protection
topic: Identification of AN-type, NAS etc.; grip length, torques, a/c bolt identification, screws, taper pins.
syllabus_extract: Identification of AN-type, NAS etc.; grip length, torques, a/c bolt identification, screws, taper pins.
specific_objectives: 25.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe the use of various standards, identification of bolts, nuts, safety methods and maintenance of cables.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Identification of AN-type, NAS, screws, and taper pins using physical samples; Safety precautions for handling fasteners; Instructor supervision during identification exercises.
intro_questions: What are the two primary standards for aircraft fasteners?
Why is grip length critical in aircraft structural assembly?
What is the primary function of a taper pin in aircraft maintenance?

development.content:
AN-type and NAS fastener identification
Grip length measurement techniques
Standard torque values for bolts

Aircraft bolt identification procedures
Screw types and applications
Taper pin specifications and usage

Safety methods for fastener handling
Proper storage and maintenance protocols
Inspection criteria for damaged fasteners

summary_questions: Differentiate between AN-type and NAS fasteners based on head markings.
Explain the relationship between grip length and thread engagement in aircraft structures.
Describe the correct procedure for selecting and installing a taper pin.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report comparing the torque specifications for AN-type bolts versus NAS bolts for a specific aircraft application covered in the next lesson plan.

pft_rows.syllabus: Nuts, miscellaneous nuts, washers, Safety methods for turn buckles and various types of turn buckles.
